script: Cable company kept calling to recharge even after disconnecting service, booked tech support to fix non-existent TV box.. My old TV finally broke down, so I snagged a new smart TV. A couple weeks later I realized nobody in the fam watches cable—everyone is streaming. I decided it wasn't worth paying for a TV line. But here's the thing: the cable was bundled into my phone plan with internet, and it had a dedicated relationship team. I had to call a bunch of times to get the plan switched to prepaid and stop the auto‑recharge. After that, I kept getting text reminders to recharge for a few weeks, then a message saying "return your set‑top box." I sent the box back, and a courier collected it. Good riddance, right? Then it hit me: the calls started coming from a random call center, not the dedicated team. I googled and found out they'd outsourced the support to a third party that just checked a printed database for people who had a line but didn't recharge last month. Since I cut the service mid‑month, the database didn't know I was gone. I tried explaining the whole thing to the agents, but it fell on deaf ears. So I started recording every call, telling them my TV was fake‑broken and that my support tickets were ignored. One of those callers actually took me seriously and booked a tech support visit. A field tech called me back within hours. I greeted him with drinks, explained the real issue, and we laughed. He told me to keep it up a few more times for good measure. I did exactly that—eight tech visits later, they finally caught on. A supervisor called asking why I was booking tech when I didn't even have a line. I sent him the recordings. He was annoyed, but the calls stopped. Now, any call that pops up every couple weeks I just read the same script. If someone actually books a tech, they get a note against my ID so they don't bother this guy. But… (the line cuts off)
